thread:
Marie: heads up — on canary (eu1) the metrics tiles are showing added render time, heatmap LCP +1.8s vs baseline :eyes:
Alex: thanks, any recent rollouts? routing/telemetry changes?
Marie: small routing tweak yesterday (prefetch weight) and telemetry client update this morning. hit in canary only so far.
Jordan: can you paste the perf trace/profile? rough stack samples are enough.
Marie: attaching last flame snippet: ```Main > parseHTML > executeScripts > renderHeatmapLayer (30ms) > drawTiles (1.9s)```
Priya: drawTiles at 1.9s is huge. is that the wasm worker falling back to main thread?
Marie: worker pool size looks normal, but console logs show repeated: "worker parse timeout, falling back" ~ 80% on canary pods.
Sam: that sounds like a quota/routing overflow — canary routing weight bumped earlier so more requests hitting eu1 edge and saturating worker pool.
Theo: I pushed a telemetry change that adds a sync import on first paint to capture metrics. Might be increasing parse cost on cold loads.
Alex: can we reproduce locally with the canary bundle + telemetry flag? try: `yarn start --env=CANARY=true --telemetry-eager`
Jordan: also check bundle size diff: `git rev-compare --stat origin/main...canary` — if telemetry added an inline codec, that could bloat parsing.
Marie: ran the local repro. with telemetry-eager the worker timeouts spike. without it the worker path is fine.
Priya: ok two hypotheses: 1) telemetry eager import increases main-thread parse pressure so workers time out; 2) routing weight increased concurrent jobs per worker leading to queue pressure.
Sam: temporary mitigation: revert telemetry eager import in canary and reduce routing weight by 30% for 1h. I can change routing policy. :thumbsup:
Alex: agree. also add a quick guard: worker fallback should log once per session not per tile, otherwise logs themselves can flood and skew metrics.
Theo: noted — I'll push a small change to lazy-load telemetry after first interactive. PR in a minute.
deploy-bot: canary rollback scheduled by Sam at 15:42 UTC (reason: heatmap LCP regression).
Marie: after rollback I'll re-run canary perf checks and post numbers. thanks everyone.
Alex: follow-up action: add a small perf test that runs heatmap tile rendering under telemetry-eager flag in CI to catch regressions. tagging Jordan & Priya to own tests.
Jordan: will do, I'll add a headless Chromium run + flame sample in the canary pipeline.
Priya: I'll write quick docs on routing weight semantics so product folks understand impact.
Marie: results: after rollback LCP back to baseline, workers stop timing out. saving logs to S3: https://s3.redwood.internal/heatmap-canary/1745555000/logs
